purpose: Manufacturer-verified HyperAccel Bertha LPU accelerator records for LLM inference, preserving announced/coming-soon status and explicitly separating vendor performance claims from independently reproduced results.

hardware.architecture: HyperAccel LPU; inference-specialized coarse-core architecture with streamlined dataflow, hardware-native batching and multi-chip scaling
hardware.model_size_practicality: 128GB base memory provides enough raw capacity for many 70B-class 4-bit models with useful headroom; 256GB configurations can accommodate substantially larger quantized models. Actual usable model size depends on runtime overhead, KV cache, context, batching and whether all memory is exposed to a given execution path.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: low_to_moderate; 250W accelerator TDP is relatively efficient for 128-256GB capacity but requires a host, cooling and external AC/DC infrastructure
hardware.efficiency_notes: Specification-derived memory capacity per accelerator watt is 0.512GB/W at 128GB and 1.024GB/W at 256GB. These are capacity ratios, not measured tokens/joule.

vendor_benchmarks_and_claims.claim: Bertha 500 supports 1024 concurrent requests and 768 TFLOPS FP8 with approximately 90% hardware utilization during inference.
vendor_benchmarks_and_claims.normalization_caveat: Utilization is a vendor architecture claim and has not been independently reproduced here.

vendor_benchmarks_and_claims.claim: Against an NVIDIA H100 comparison, HyperAccel reports 1,645 vs 804 tokens/s, 411,225 vs 22,970 tokens/s per $1M and 13,700 vs 1,149 tokens/s/kW.
vendor_benchmarks_and_claims.normalization_caveat: Model, quantization, serving settings, system configuration and price basis are not sufficiently disclosed for normalized cross-platform ranking; retain as vendor evidence only.

pricing.note: No public numeric MSRP or broadly orderable retail price was verified. HyperAccel provides an inquiry path.

source_caveats: HyperAccel public materials describe B500 samples in 2026 and mass production targeted for 2027; status is therefore not recorded as generally available.
No independent retail price or independently reproduced end-to-end LLM benchmark was verified in this pass.

hardware.architecture: HyperAccel LPU-based edge SoC/accelerator for multimodal inference
hardware.model_size_practicality: 16GB places B100 primarily in the small-to-mid local model tier. Roughly 7B-14B quantized workloads are plausible by capacity, but real fit depends on model format, context, KV cache and HyperDex support.
hardware.off_grid_suitability: potentially_high_pending_power_disclosure; compact M.2 format and LPDDR5X target edge deployments, but HyperAccel does not publish a final B100 board/system power figure on the current product page
hardware.efficiency_notes: HyperAccel positions B100 for IoT, smart appliances and on-premise edge systems; do not infer watts or tokens/joule from the architecture-level LPU IP figures.

pricing.note: No public numeric MSRP or retail listing verified. Product page states Coming Q4, 2026.

source_caveats: The current B100 product page states 32.768 TFLOPS FP8, while descriptive marketing text also references a rounded 48 TFLOPS balanced specification. This record uses the explicit specification table value and preserves the discrepancy here.
A final B100 accelerator TDP, public MSRP and independent LLM tokens/s benchmark were not verified.
